name: Vigo
title: Vigo Ship UTM | Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging in Galicia
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Vigo: shipyard dockings, fishing fleet, car carriers and cruise ships, hull, tank and scrubber piping gauging in the ría.
h1: Vigo Hull Gauging: Thickness Measurement in Galicia's Biggest Repair Port
intro: Vigo is the busiest ship-repair and fishing centre on Spain's Atlantic coast, with several yards, floating docks and a harbour that serves fishing fleets, car carriers, container ships and cruise vessels. For gauging it is the place where afloat readings turn into docking work. Our ultrasonic thickness technicians travel from India to the ship, measuring hull, tanks and piping at the yard, the quay or the anchorage.

highlights.h: Yards and floating docks in the ría
highlights.p: Vigo's repair yards run floating docks and long quays, so a ship can be gauged afloat, then docked in the same stay. Readings feed the steel list while repairs are still being scoped.
Large trawlers, freezer vessels and fish-carrying ships use Vigo constantly. Their hulls and fish-hold boundaries suffer hard wear, which makes thickness records valuable before a refit.
Vehicle carriers loading at the port and cruise ships calling at the transatlantic quay give short windows for deck, tank and scrubber piping readings between operations.

port.h: The Ría de Vigo and its working harbour
p: Vigo stands on the southern shore of a deep, sheltered ría in Galicia, protected from the Atlantic by the Cíes Islands at its mouth. The geography is the port's asset: ships anchor and berth in calm water close to a city whose economy has long depended on the sea. Berths run along the waterfront from the old fishing quays and the cruise terminal to the container, vehicle and general cargo facilities further out, and the shipbuilding and repair yards sit on both sides of the ría, with a steady stream of small craft crossing between them.

Fishing is the defining trade. The port lands more fish than any other in Europe by most accounts, serving a large distant-water fleet of trawlers and freezer ships along with a coastal fleet, and a cluster of cold-chain and processing firms depends on it. Alongside the fishing vessels, car carriers load vehicles built at the plant in the Vigo area, container ships and feeders call at the terminal on the southern side, and cruise ships berth at the central quays. Ro-ro, general cargo and bulk ships call for the region's industries, and offshore and research vessels use the yards for maintenance.

For gauging, Vigo's mix is attractive because many types of ship pass through a short stretch of water. A trawler hauled for refit, a car carrier waiting for its next cargo, a cruise ship on a short call and a general cargo ship in for repairs each have a different pattern of wear and a different window for the work. Fishing vessels often show wastage around fish holds, in ballast and fuel tanks and at the shell where ice or gear has rubbed. Car carriers show wear on ramps and vehicle decks, and cruise ships bring concern about scrubber piping and tanks, so the programme is chosen ship by ship.

facilities.h: Yards, quays and anchorages where gauging happens
p: The yards are the centre of Vigo's gauging work. Metalships & Docks operates floating docks and a long repair quay on the ría and takes mid-sized merchant ships, offshore vessels and fishing ships; several other yards, among them Freire, Armón and Barreras, build and repair vessels from small to large. A dock stay gives full access to the bottom and side shell, and the superintendent usually wants renewal-survey and condition readings completed before steel orders are placed. We work to the yard's sequence and report compartment by compartment, so the steel list can be revised as tanks are cleaned and released.

Outside the yards, gauging is done alongside at the fishing quays, the vehicle and container terminals and the cruise berths, or at the anchorage in the ría, where launches reach ships waiting for a berth or for orders. The sheltered water makes anchorage boarding easier than on most Atlantic harbours, and holds and ballast tanks on an idle bulk or general cargo ship can be measured while it waits. Equipment travels with the technicians, including magnetic particle yokes for cracks at frame ends, hatch corners and welded attachments found during the readings.
list: Metalships & Docks, Vigo — dry-dock and afloat gauging on merchant, offshore and fishing vessels around its floating docks
Other ría yards (Freire, Armón, Barreras) — newbuild, conversion and repair gauging as each yard's programme allows
Fishing port quays — hull, fish-hold boundary and tank gauging on trawlers and freezer vessels in port
Vehicle terminal berths — ramp, vehicle deck and ballast tank gauging on car carriers between cargoes
Container terminal and general cargo quays — deck, hatch coaming and ballast tank readings on short-sea and feeder ships
Cruise quays and the ría anchorage — tank, piping and scrubber readings, and launch-served work on waiting ships

context.h: Spanish maritime administration and the pressures on Vigo's fleet
p: Port state control in Vigo falls under the Paris MoU and is carried out by the Spanish maritime administration, the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante, through the Capitanía Marítima in the port. Inspectors target older ships and those with a poor record, and Vigo's mix of long-serving fishing tonnage and visiting merchant ships provides plenty of candidates. A superintendent who has taken thickness readings before arrival is less likely to be surprised by a structural deficiency raised during an inspection, and has time to plan repair work around the stay.

Obligations under EU law add pressure. Every ship that calls here also needs an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, as the EU recycling rules for ships demand, while the emissions trading scheme has reached shipping from 2024 and FuelEU Maritime from 2025. Fishing vessels are covered by their own fleet rules and safety regimes, and owners who intend to extend a vessel's life often seek independent thickness records before committing to major steel renewal. For merchant ships, the same readings support sale and purchase, charter on and off-hire checks and the planning of the next docking, whichever yard is chosen.

jobs.p: Vigo's work is yard-led for larger ships and quay-led for the busy fishing and vehicle trades. The superintendent or owner sends the survey status, the repair specification and any earlier gauging report, and we agree which compartments are available and in what order. The team travels from India once the dock slot or the call date is firm, and where possible the same technicians cover the afloat readings and the docked stage. Typical requests include:
list: Renewal-survey gauging on a general cargo ship in dock at a ría yard, covering hold frames, tank tops, ballast tanks and hatch coamings.
Hull, fish-hold boundary and ballast tank gauging on a freezer trawler hauled out for refit, to size steel renewal before work begins.
Ramp and vehicle-deck plating readings on a car carrier between cargoes at the vehicle terminal, ahead of an intermediate survey.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging on a cruise ship during a call, for owners planning maintenance.
A pre-docking steel estimate taken on a bulk carrier at anchor in the ría, with the list sent to the yard before the dock slot starts.

logistics: The nearest airport is Vigo-Peinador, with additional routes through Santiago de Compostela, A Coruña or Porto; technicians usually connect through Madrid or Lisbon from India. Spain is in the Schengen area, so each technician needs a visa obtained in India, applied for once the dock slot or call is confirmed and supported by an invitation naming the vessel. The ship's agent arranges port passes and launches, while each yard issues its own site access. Dock dates move, so flights are confirmed against the yard's latest schedule.

faqs.q: Can gauging be done in a floating dock at Vigo?
faqs.a: Yes. Floating docks give access to the bottom and side shell once the ship is blocked, and we measure after the yard has cleaned the surface. We coordinate with the dock master and the yard's work sequence, because the dock is often wanted for the next ship, and we report compartment by compartment so renewals can be decided during the stay.

faqs.q: Is a fishing trawler gauged the same way as a merchant ship?
faqs.a: Yes. Fishing vessels are measured in the same way as other ships, with particular attention to fish-hold boundaries, ballast and fuel tanks, the shell at the waterline and areas worn by gear or ice. Owners use the readings to size steel renewal at refit or to support a sale or life-extension decision.

faqs.q: Is the ría anchorage suitable for gauging?
faqs.a: Often, because the water is sheltered by the Cíes Islands. A launch from the agent takes the team to a ship waiting for a berth or orders, and ballast tanks, deck plating and empty holds can be measured. Cargo tanks on tankers are left for a gas-free stay, and we confirm access and safety with the master.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at Vigo before it goes to a different yard?
faqs.a: Yes. Readings taken at Vigo, at the quay or at anchor, become a measured steel list that you can send to any yard, in Galicia or elsewhere, so the repair estimate is based on actual plate rather than on the last survey report. Telling us the target yard helps us format the report to match.

faqs.q: What lead time is needed for a gauging job at Vigo?
faqs.a: As early as the ship's schedule is known. Visas for the technicians take time to arrange, and a dock slot or planned call gives us room to complete them and agree the scope. Short-notice requests are still worth sending, and we will say honestly whether a team can reach the ship in time.
